title: SharePoint admin center: Data access governance report of sites a group can access
summary: Hold: Microsoft Learn now documents the group report, including its admin steps, PowerShell automation, licensing and limits, which this briefing still reports as unpublished. Administrators would miss the Groups option and the documented snapshot-report entitlement.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns SharePoint.
claims.quote: "products": ["SharePoint"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a report showing every site a given group can access.
claims.quote: With this new report, SharePoint admins can now see every site a group can access and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: The planned report shows the extent of the group's access.
claims.quote: SharePoint admins can now see every site a group can access and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: The roadmap warns that broad-membership groups and vendor groups can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.
claims.quote: A single group with broad membership or a special group for vendors etc. - can expose sensitive content to unintended recipients.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The notice places the new group report in Data access governance in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: We are introducing a new Data access governance report in the SharePoint admin center that allows SharePoint administrators to identify all sites accessible to a given group and the extent of that access.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the group report and its overview lists no report for groups.
claims.quote: Site permissions for users or groups report: Lists all sites a specified user or group can access and the extent of that access. Each report contains either users or groups, not both.
claims.fix: Replace the documentation-absence statements with 'Microsoft Learn now documents the Site permissions for users or groups snapshot report, with separate user and group reports.' Retain the roadmap status and Message Center rollout window as separately attributed plans.

claims.claim: The user report lists all sites a specified user can access.
claims.quote: For each user or group, it lists all accessible sites and shows whether the entire site is shared or access is limited to specific files or folders.

claims.claim: The user report distinguishes access to the entire site from access limited to sections of it.
claims.quote: shows whether the entire site is shared or access is limited to specific files or folders.

claims.claim: User reports include items shared directly with the user.
claims.quote: For users, the report includes counts of items shared directly with the user and items accessible indirectly through group membership.

claims.claim: User reports include items accessible indirectly through group membership.
claims.quote: For users, the report includes counts of items shared directly with the user and items accessible indirectly through group membership.

claims.claim: A per-user report answers a user-access question rather than reporting directly on a group.
claims.quote: Each report contains either users or groups, not both.

claims.claim: Neither the group report's admin UI nor its PowerShell automation is documented.
claims.quote: Retrieve the groups with Get-MgGroup, then pass the returned group objects directly to the TargetGroups parameter.
claims.fix: Populate the existing row's UI with 'Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users or groups > View reports > Create report > Create report for > Groups' using https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report. Populate its API with 'Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name <name> -TargetGroups <groups>' and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/powershell-for-data-access-governance. State in the note that <groups> means group objects returned by Get-MgGroup, and that the guide documents TargetGroups while the cmdlet reference currently omits it. Remove the corresponding documentation-absence prose and open question.

claims.claim: The SharePoint admin center path to Data access governance is Reports > Data access governance.
claims.quote: In the left pane, expand Reports and then select Data access governance.

claims.claim: Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity <entity> lists existing Data access governance reports.
claims.quote:
Lists various 'Data Access Governance' (DAG) reports in SharePoint admin center.
Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to access Data access governance using SharePoint administrator credentials.
claims.quote: Sign in to the SharePoint admin center with the SharePoint administrator credentials for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft documentation does not show that Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight supports the group report.
claims.quote:
Use the following command to check user and group permission reports:
Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport
claims.fix: Replace 'does not show the group report is supported' and the matching prose with 'The PowerShell guide documents Get-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport for reviewing user and group permission reports.' Use https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/powershell-for-data-access-governance as the supporting citation.

claims.claim: The user report path is Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users > View reports > Create report.
claims.quote:
From the Data access governance landing page, select View reports under Site permissions for users or groups.
Select Create report to generate your report.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Reports > Data access governance > Site permissions for users or groups > View reports > Create report > Create report for > Users'. The renamed report and Users choice are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report.

claims.claim: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight accepts PermissionsReport, Snapshot, SharePoint, Name and UserPrincipalNames for the user report.
claims.quote:
UserPermissionsParameterSet
Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight
    -ReportEntity <ReportEntityEnum>
    -Workload <WorkloadEnum>
    -ReportType <ReportTypeEnum>
    -Name <String>
    -UserPrincipalNames <System.Collections.Generic.List`1[System.String]>

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide uses -UserEmailList for the user report.
claims.quote: Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight -ReportEntity PermissionsReport -ReportType Snapshot -Workload SharePoint -Name "UserSharePointReport" -UserEmailList "a@contoso.com","b@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference instead documents -UserPrincipalNames.
claims.quote:
-UserPrincipalNames
Specifies the user principal names of the users for whom permissions report should be generated.

claims.claim: The PowerShell guide says UserEmailList requires user principal names.
claims.quote: While the parameter is named UserEmailList, the report requires user principal names.

claims.claim: The Start cmdlet reference includes PermissionsReport and PermissionedUsers as ReportEntity values.
claims.quote: Accepted values: Everyone, EveryoneExceptExternalUsers, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersAtSite, EveryoneExceptExternalUsersForItems, PermissionedUsers, PermissionsReport, SensitivityLabelForFiles, SharingLinks_Anyone, SharingLinks_Guests, SharingLinks_PeopleInYourOrg

claims.claim: The Start cmdlet reference lists no group-specific parameter set.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint site permissions for users or groups report group PowerShell GroupId GroupIds ReportEntity licensing default automatic. Read Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight and powershell-for-data-access-governance: only the guide documents TargetGroups.
claims.fix: Replace the reference-only absence sentence with 'The PowerShell guide documents -TargetGroups, although the Start-SPODataAccessGovernanceInsight reference currently omits it.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/powershell-for-data-access-governance alongside the existing cmdlet reference.

claims.claim: The documented user report can be downloaded as CSV.
claims.quote: To download a CSV file for a specific user or group, select that recipient and use the download link above the site list.

claims.claim: The group report's output format is not documented.
claims.quote: Select Download report for all groups in a group report, or Download detailed report in a user report, to get a ZIP file containing CSV files for all recipients included in the report.
claims.fix: Replace 'the group report's output format is not yet documented' with 'the group report supports CSV download for a selected group and ZIP download containing CSV files for all included groups', citing https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/data-access-governance-site-permissions-users-report.

claims.claim: Microsoft lists nonpseudonymized report data as a possible cause of Data access governance reports not working.
claims.quote: Reports might not work if you select nonpseudonymized report data for your organization.

claims.claim: The group report's licensing model is unknown and no Microsoft page establishes its entitlement.
claims.quote: The Site permissions for users or groups report is one of the Data access governance snapshot reports available with SharePoint Advanced Management.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'mixed'. Replace the licensing-absence notes, body caveats, checklist caveat and rationale premise with 'The group report is a SharePoint Advanced Management snapshot report. The SAM prerequisites provide entitlement through at least one assigned Microsoft Copilot licence, SharePoint K/P1/P2 plus the SAM Plan 1 add-on, or Microsoft 365 E7, with the listed base subscription. Microsoft 365 E5 alone does not provide snapshot reports.' Cite the already listed report, prerequisites and overview pages. Remove the open question about whether its licence is published; retain the existing exact base-plan list.
